# R145B — Exact shifted-extremal projection width and finite global-minimum sweep

Date: 2026-11-14 (Asia/Shanghai). Status: AUTHOR-SIDE EXACT SPECIAL-FAMILY PROOF AND FINITE EXHAUSTIVE RESULT; NOT_REVIEWED.
Frozen science pin: \`43ec6098b1330ae86d0a7863be336c5d97f6ef34\`.
Scope: external tied-phase scalar S23 finite mechanical words, without X6 identification.
Scientific predecessor: R143 convex projection/residue proof @ \`84863c21633962404531ecce89a5abab85e8162a\`; R139B sharp extremal-word threshold @ \`419b3f1f0b732cb945a51b3b9e33406449fe6b81\`.

## 1. Exact projected interval width

Let w be a length-m binary word with prefix sums s_j. Its free-intercept slope support is (\alpha_w,\beta_w), with
\[
\alpha_w=\max(0,\max_{i<j}(s_j-s_i-1)/(j-i)),\quad
\beta_w=\min(1,\min_{i<j}(s_j-s_i+1)/(j-i)).
\]
Define
\[
u_w(t)=\min_{0\le j\le m}(s_j+1-jt),\qquad
\ell_w(t)=\max_{0\le j\le m}(s_j-jt).
\]
R143's exact projection theorem identifies the open interval of phase indices N via
\[
I_w(L)=\bigl(L\alpha_w-u_w(\alpha_w),\,L\beta_w-\ell_w(\beta_w)\bigr),\quad L=K-1\ge1.
\]
Its width is
\[
\mathcal D_w(L)=L(\beta_w-\alpha_w)+u_w(\alpha_w)-\ell_w(\beta_w).
\]
If \(\mathcal D_w(L)>1\), an integer lies strictly inside \(I_w(L)\), so w is present in the tied-phase observer at K=L+1. This is an elementary sufficient membership condition independent of the fractional part of the endpoint.

## 2. R145B.1: universal explicit shifted-extremal width

For every integer m>=6, consider the length-m word
\[
v_m=1\,0^{m-3}\,1\,0.
\]
The exact prefix-pair support and endpoint intercepts are
\[
\boxed{\alpha_{v_m}=\frac1{m-1},\quad\beta_{v_m}=\frac1{m-3},\quad
u_{v_m}(\alpha_{v_m})=1,\quad
\ell_{v_m}(\beta_{v_m})=1-\frac1{m-3}.}
\]
Consequently, for every integer L>=1,
\[
\boxed{\mathcal D_{v_m}(L)=\frac{2L+m-1}{(m-1)(m-3)}.}\tag{1}
\]
The bitwise complement has exactly the same projected width, by the slope reflection and intercept-coordinate symmetry.

**Proof.** The word v_m has ones at positions 0 and m-2. Among all contiguous subwords, the largest forced lower slope comes from the shortest segment containing both ones: length m-1, giving \alpha=1/(m-1). The smallest forced upper slope comes from the longest zero-only segment, positions 1,...,m-3, length m-3, giving \beta=1/(m-3). For m>=6 all other intervals yield weaker constraints (one-one upper bounds are at least 2/(m-1), and empty lower bounds are nonpositive). At t=\alpha, the j=0 upper-intercept line gives u<=1 and all other lines give >=1; hence u(\alpha)=1. At t=\beta, j=1 gives \ell>=1-\beta and all other lines give <=1-\beta; hence \ell(\beta)=1-\beta. Substitution yields (1). Complementing w maps slope t to 1-t and bijects integer phase-index line crossings under t to 1-t, so it preserves the projected interval length. QED.

Put
\[
E(m)=(m-2)\left\lfloor\frac{m-1}{2}\right\rfloor+1,\qquad L_*=E(m)-1.
\]
Then (1) simplifies to
\[
\boxed{\mathcal D_{v_m}(L_*)=
\begin{cases}
1+\dfrac{m}{(m-1)(m-3)},&m\ge6\text{ even},\\[2mm]
1+\dfrac{2}{m-3},&m\ge7\text{ odd}.
\end{cases}}\tag{2}
\]
Thus this entire infinite nonextremal family is realized at K=E(m), with quantitative strict margin above 1.

## 3. R145B.2: exact finite exhaustive minimal-width certificates

Independent rational Farey-cell enumeration \`check_r145b.py\` enumerates the complete finite Sturmian language W_m for **every m=5,...,30**, crosschecks its cardinality with the totient formula
\(1+\sum_{q=1}^{m}(m+1-q)\varphi(q)\),
and evaluates the exact R143 projected width at L=E(m)-1 for every word except the two extreme patterns \(10^{m-2}1\) and \(01^{m-2}0\).

It checked 26 full lengths and **24,924 nonextremal word-width pairs**, using Python's exact \`Fraction\` arithmetic. Every checked width is >1.

The exact global minima have the following verified finite descriptions:
- m=5: minimum 4/3, attained by \`00101\` and its complement \`11010\` (the shifted-extremal formula (2) is not the minimum here).
- m=6: minimum 7/5, attained by v_6 and its complement.
- m=7: minimum 3/2, attained by v_7 and its complement **and** the reflected/reversed pair \`0001001\`, \`1110110\` (four minimizers).
- Every m=8,...,30: the minimum equals the value (2) and is attained **only by v_m and its bitwise complement**.

The accompanying \`verification_r145b.json\` contains every length, word count, exact minimum, the closed-form value and complete minimizing-word strings. Program marker: \`R145B_SHIFTED_EXTREMAL_FINITE_PASS\`.

## 4. Next theorem obligation

The finite data motivate the following **unproved full-length proposition**: for all m>=8, every nonextremal Sturmian word w satisfies \(\mathcal D_w(E(m)-1)\ge \mathcal D_{v_m}(E(m)-1)>1\).

A proof, plus the direct finite base lengths m=5..7, would imply every nonextremal word occurs at every K>=E(m), since \(\mathcal D_w(L)\) is strictly increasing in L. The two extremal words are handled exactly by R139B's quotient-and-remainder criterion; thus this would prove the conjectural optimal eventual saturation threshold T(m)=E(m) for all m>=5. The finite sweep supplies evidence for a precise inequality, not the universal inequality itself.

The parent R145 conservation identities, retained phase multiplicity and Source research scope remain unchanged.
